rawCandidates.selectionReason: Tutor-discovery hero maps directly to a parent choosing a subject and taking one next step.
Education brand system with playful geometry can make tutoring feel less remedial.
High-consideration education page with session detail, bullet clarity, and dated program module.
Guided catalog prompt and subject chips are useful for routing parents by exam, confidence, or weekly support need.
Learning shelf structure helps show program options, but its image dependency is risky for this fixture.
Proof stats and subject cards are useful as anti-claim warnings and as a structural reference.
Custom introduction CTA band maps to request-a-diagnostic-call without pretending instant booking.
Soft artifact collage is a model for showing diagnostic notes and progress planning without student photos.
Service-provider proof overlays are useful as a warning against fake ratings and prices.
Editorial independent-professional hero offers a crafted alternative to generic school-site styling.
Client-portal artifact can become a parent-facing study plan and next-action proof block.
Parent-safety language and soft educational layout fit the privacy-sensitive tutoring decision.
Parent-control resource section shows how to turn anxiety into a calm explain-and-choose flow.
Parent-guide resource cards are a strong model for consultation prep content and plain help links.
Education hub page shows careful parent support copy with a mobile preview artifact.
Privacy-control page is useful for tone and governance, not visual identity.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Make the first decision a parent diagnostic request for maths support, not a generic education browse moment.
Hero should route by need: weekly support, exam prep, or confidence rebuilding.
Use one dominant enquire CTA with a quieter subject/need selector nearby.
Collapse selector, trust cue, and CTA into large stacked mobile controls.

bannedUses: Do not copy Preply's marketplace, tutor counts, reviews, learner labels, portrait stack, or find-your-tutor language.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use warm academic color blocks as orientation cues, not a one-note school-blue palette.
Simple geometric shapes can make maths feel approachable without cartooning the business.
Use equation grids, paper slips, and progress markers instead of child stock photos.
If no approved student/tutor photos exist, lead with privacy-safe learning artifacts.

bannedUses: Do not copy SuperHi's discount banner, learner counts, smiley mascot, exact geometric composition, or creative-career promise.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Spell out the tutoring path: diagnostic call, support plan, weekly sessions, parent check-ins.
Use process proof and source-backed lesson structure instead of exam-result promises.
A date/session module can explain availability or intake windows without requiring a full booking system.
Use Toronto school-year, exam, and parent-call language only when source-backed by the business packet.

bannedUses: Do not copy bootcamp dates, industry-expert claims, certification claims, countdown offers, or reserve-seat pressure.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: A guided prompt can ask what the student is stuck on before routing to an enquiry.
Lead form should capture year level, exam goal, parent concern, and preferred contact path.
Need selected, missing, error, and submitted states for the parent enquiry path.
Subject chips and form prompts need visible labels, keyboard focus, and large touch targets.

bannedUses: Do not copy Codecademy's AI course prompt, topic taxonomy, bootcamp promotion, or certification prep labels.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: A dark introduction band can separate the parent call from lesson detail without adding decorative cards.
Keep depth low: section contrast and spacing should carry hierarchy before shadows.
Use spacious sections around parent concerns so the page feels calm, not salesy.
Pair quiet body copy with firm section titles for reassurance and scan speed.

bannedUses: Do not copy Sana's enterprise logos, corporate learning claims, or book-a-custom-introduction wording.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Write with calm expert confidence: parent problem, next step, no inflated academic outcomes.
Use a strong left-led headline with a right-side diagnostic artifact instead of generic tutor portraits.
Visible service categories should map to same-URL or fallback agent-readable facts for tutoring, exam prep, and consultations.
Tokenize headline scale, artifact border, accent color, and form spacing so variants stay governable.

bannedUses: Do not copy Contra Pro pricing, wallet/pro profile cards, invite-only waitlist, or holographic graphics.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: A static study-plan artifact can replace heavy video, dashboard embeds, or private student imagery.
If motion is used, limit it to selected concern or step reveal; no distracting animated education theater.
Use utility icons only for year level, exam, call, and study plan cues.
Hide portal-like claims unless parent accounts, privacy rules, and data handling are real.

bannedUses: Do not copy Copilot's SaaS trial language, client portal promise, app-store screenshot, or firm automation claims.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Address parent anxiety directly: what happens on the call, what is private, and what support looks like.
Privacy-safe parent/student visuals must be owner-approved; otherwise use abstract learning materials.
Warm safety color can be used sparingly for reassurance, while CTAs stay disciplined.
Avoid all claims about grades, guaranteed confidence, credentials, safeguarding, or results unless the business supplies proof.

bannedUses: Do not copy YouTube Kids branding, app-download CTA, child imagery, safety claims, or family-friendly platform proof.

antiReferences.rejectionReason: Huge tutor counts, star ratings, and subject availability proof would become fabricated trust claims for a local tutoring fixture.
Revenue-growth percentages and marketplace acquisition claims are irrelevant and unsafe for parent-facing tutoring.
Generic AI service-card layout would make Maple Row feel template-made and weak on parent trust.
Safety-control framing is too platform-compliance-heavy and would overstate tutoring privacy infrastructure.

remixDirection.summary: A parent-first maths tutoring page with a calm diagnostic-call hero, privacy-safe learning artifacts, clear need routing, process proof, and a short enquiry path for weekly support, exam prep, or confidence rebuilding.
selectedMoves: Preply-inspired subject/need selector, rebuilt as a local diagnostic-call enquiry instead of tutor marketplace search.
SuperHi-inspired approachable geometry, adapted into maths paper, grid, and progress artifacts.
Codecademy-inspired program clarity for the tutoring path and parent decision modules.
Sana-inspired introduction CTA band for the diagnostic call handoff.
Copilot-inspired artifact proof, rebuilt as a static study-plan preview without portal claims.
YouTube Kids-inspired parent-anxiety framing, stripped of child imagery and safety-platform claims.
explicitRejects: No invented grades, guaranteed outcomes, reviews, tutor counts, credentials, safeguarding claims, student photos, or parent testimonials.
No marketplace language, SaaS trial language, school-system authority claims, or exact layout copy.
Do not show student work, names, ages, marks, or private parent details unless supplied and approved.
